notes.meaning: Early on Sunday morning, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb while it was still dark outside to care for Jesus' body. When she arrived, she was surprised to find that the heavy stone sealing the entrance had already been taken away.
Mary ran back to find Simon Peter and John to tell them the news. She assumed someone had stolen or moved the Lord's body, never imagining that He had risen from the dead.

Peter and John rushed toward the tomb right away to see what had happened for themselves. John ran faster than Peter and reached the tomb first, driven by his deep love and eager desire to know the truth.
John bent down to look through the low entrance of the tomb. He could see the linen burial cloths lying on the ground, but he paused outside and did not go in.

Peter arrived right behind John and boldly walked straight into the tomb. He saw the linen wraps lying there and noticed the head cloth rolled up by itself in an orderly way, showing that no rushed grave robbers had taken the body.
Encouraged by Peter's boldness, John went inside the tomb as well. When he saw the undisturbed burial cloths, he understood that Jesus was alive and believed.

Up to this moment, the disciples had not understood the Old Testament prophecies that said the Messiah had to rise from the dead. Their grief and human weakness had kept them from grasping the promise of Scripture.
After examining the empty tomb, Peter and John returned to their lodgings. They went home unsure of what would happen next, waiting for God to make things clear.
Mary stayed behind outside the tomb, weeping because she thought her Lord was lost. As she cried, she bent down to look into the tomb once more.

Mary saw two angels dressed in bright white clothing sitting where the body of Jesus had rested, one at the head and one at the feet. Their presence honored the risen Lord and prepared her to meet Him.

The angels asked Mary why she was crying, gently hinting that she had a reason for joy rather than sorrow. She answered that she was weeping because someone had taken her Lord away and she did not know where to find Him.
Mary turned around and saw a man standing near her who was actually Jesus, but she did not recognize Him. Her heavy grief and tear-filled eyes kept her from realizing that her Lord was alive.

Jesus asked Mary why she was crying and whom she was seeking, speaking kindly to her troubled heart. Assuming He was the gardener, she offered to carry the Lord's body away herself if He would only tell her where it was.
Jesus called her by name with His familiar and loving voice. That single word opened Mary's eyes at once, and she turned and cried out with joy, calling Him her Master.

Jesus told Mary not to cling to Him, because He had not yet ascended to heaven and was not staying to resume His earthly life as before. Instead, He sent her to tell His disciples, warmly calling them His brothers and assuring them that His Father was now their Father.

Mary Magdalene went straight to the disciples and announced that she had seen the Lord. She faithfully delivered everything Jesus had told her, becoming the first witness sent to proclaim His resurrection.

On that Sunday evening, the disciples gathered behind locked doors because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders. Jesus came and stood right in their midst, giving them His blessing of peace to calm their fears.

Jesus showed the disciples His pierced hands and wounded side so they would know He had a real, risen body. Seeing the physical proof that He was truly their crucified Lord filled the disciples with great joy.

Jesus gave the disciples His peace a second time to prepare them for their high calling. Just as the Father had sent Jesus into the world, Jesus was now sending His followers out as His appointed ambassadors.

Jesus breathed on the disciples, echoing how God breathed life into man at creation. By this symbolic act, He gave them a foretaste of the Holy Spirit to renew their hearts and equip them for their ministry.

Jesus commissioned His disciples to proclaim the terms of God's forgiveness. When they preach that sins are pardoned through faith in Christ, God stands behind their word, and those who reject the message remain guilty.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics believe Jesus gave the apostles and their successors the authority to forgive or withhold forgiveness in the sacrament of confession, which requires confessing specific sins to a priest.

notes.meaning: Thomas was missing from the gathering when Jesus appeared that evening. By staying away from his fellow believers, he missed out on the joy and assurance of seeing the risen Lord.

The other disciples told Thomas with joy that they had seen the Lord. Thomas stubbornly refused to believe them, insisting that he would never believe unless he could see and touch the nail holes and the wound in Jesus' side.
A week later, on the next Sunday, the disciples were together again indoors, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came and stood among them despite the closed doors, once more greeting them with peace.

Jesus spoke directly to Thomas, repeating the exact tests Thomas had demanded when he was alone. With great kindness, Jesus offered him the physical proof he asked for and urged him to stop doubting and believe.
Overcome by seeing Jesus, Thomas cried out in adoration, calling Him his Lord and his God. He made a clear confession of Jesus' divinity, and Jesus accepted this worship.
Jesus told Thomas that he believed because he had seen Him with his own eyes. He then pronounced a special blessing on everyone who would believe in Him without ever seeing Him physically.
Jesus worked many other miraculous signs in front of His disciples that are not written down in this book. John selected only the specific signs needed to build faith in Christ.

John wrote down these specific events so that readers would believe that Jesus is the promised Messiah and the Son of God. By putting their faith in Him, believers receive eternal life through His name.
